request.prompt_text:
You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,
how they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,
and in what order the thing goes together.

You receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.

WHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT
Geometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies
touch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a
part is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and
no axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not
exist yet. Saying "the axis points +Z" is this stage's work. Saying "the axis is
40 mm from the base" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.

RULES
1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a
   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give
   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group
   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four
   groups and four joints, not one region.
2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of
   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.
3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify it
   as CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION. A body pair
   that meets and is left unclassified is a hole in the design.
4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism
   can be in that matter to its function.
5. DISPOSITION EVERY DEGREE OF FREEDOM. You are given the complete list below,
   one line per rigid group per configuration per DOF. Every line gets exactly
   one of:
     INTENDED             - this motion is the point
     BLOCKED_BY           - something stops it; say WHAT, in WHICH DIRECTION,
                            and HOW A TEST WOULD DEFEAT IT, and WHY it must be
                            blocked (LOAD, KINEMATIC_NECESSITY or
                            DECLARED_SCENARIO)
     MAINTAINED_BY_CLASS  - the joint class holds it by construction
     IRRELEVANT_BECAUSE   - name a scenario in which this DOF is BOTH unloaded
                            AND unactuated. If you cannot name one, it is not
                            irrelevant.
   Leaving a line out is the failure this stage exists to prevent.
6. For every LOAD CASE, trace the ordered PATH from where the load is applied,
   through THIS mechanism, to the reaction site. Each hop names a body or joint.
   A path that does not reach the reaction site is a load that is not reacted.
   Do not state how much load any element carries: that depends on dimensions
   that do not exist.
7. Give the ASSEMBLY ORDER. For each step: which body, from which ACCESS SIDE,
   what it depends on, and - if that body must stay put afterwards - which
   RETENTION TERMINATION holds it: LATER_BODY_COVER, ROTATION or ELASTICITY. A
   rigid part pushed straight in always leaves the reverse direction open, so
   one of those three is always needed. Mark the step DEFORMATION_RESOLVED if it
   only goes together because something flexes; otherwise RIGID.
8. Name the FUNCTIONAL REGIONS the design promises: ACCESS, SUPPORT, KEEP_OUT,
   APERTURE, and which bodies own them.
9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be
empty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.

  bodies[]             id "BOD-0001", role, instance_identity
  rigid_groups[]       id "RGP-0001", body, members[], is_default (boolean)
  joints[]             id "JNT-0001", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,
                       dof[], axis_direction,
                       compliance {mode, direction, required_travel,
                       allowable_travel_status, actuation, compliant_element,
                       root_interface, activation_window} (only for COMPLIANT)
  interfaces[]         id "IFC-0001", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal_status
  configurations[]     id "CFG-0001", name, kind, bodies_present[]
  dof_dispositions[]   rigid_group, configuration, dof, disposition,
                       blocked_direction / blocker_body / defeat_specification /
                       driver   (all four required when BLOCKED_BY),
                       scenario  (required when IRRELEVANT_BECAUSE),
                       holding_class (required when MAINTAINED_BY_CLASS)
  load_paths[]         id "LDP-0001", load_case, candidate, ordered_hops[]
  assembly_steps[]     id "ASM-0001", order_index (integer), body, access_side,
                       activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  functional_regions[] id "FRG-0001", role, owning_bodies[]
  unresolved[]         id "UNR-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                       alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

PERMITTED VALUES
  joint_type          REVOLUTE | PRISMATIC | HELICAL | SPHERICAL | PLANAR | CYLINDRICAL | FIXED | COMPLIANT
  dof                 TX | TY | TZ | RX | RY | RZ
  axis_direction      +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z
  interaction_kind    CONTACT | CLEARANCE | INTERFERENCE_FIT | COMPLIANT_INTERACTION
  disposition         INTENDED | BLOCKED_BY | MAINTAINED_BY_CLASS | IRRELEVANT_BECAUSE
  driver              LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  termination_strategy LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY
  path_kind           RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  functional region role ACCESS | SUPPORT | KEEP_OUT | APERTURE
  alternatives_kind   ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

REFERENCES BETWEEN ITEMS
  rigid_groups[].body            a body id you emit
  joints[].parent_group/child_group  rigid group ids you emit
  interfaces[].bodies            body ids you emit
  configurations[].bodies_present body ids you emit
  load_paths[].load_case         a LoadCase id from the input
  load_paths[].candidate         the candidate id from the input
  load_paths[].ordered_hops      body or joint ids you emit
  assembly_steps[].body          a body id you emit
  assembly_steps[].depends_on    assembly step ids you emit
  functional_regions[].owning_bodies body ids you emit
  unresolved[].kept_open_by      Ambiguity or Freedom ids from the input

request.prompt_text:
You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,
how they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,
and in what order the thing goes together.

You receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.

WHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT
Geometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies
touch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a
part is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and
no axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not
exist yet. Saying "the axis points +Z" is this stage's work. Saying "the axis is
40 mm from the base" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.

RULES
1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a
   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give
   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group
   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four
   groups and four joints, not one region.
2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of
   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.
3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify it
   as CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION. A body pair
   that meets and is left unclassified is a hole in the design.
4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism
   can be in that matter to its function.
5. DISPOSITION EVERY DEGREE OF FREEDOM. You are given the complete list below,
   one line per rigid group per configuration per DOF. Every line gets exactly
   one of:
     INTENDED             - this motion is the point
     BLOCKED_BY           - something stops it; say WHAT, in WHICH DIRECTION,
                            and HOW A TEST WOULD DEFEAT IT, and WHY it must be
                            blocked (LOAD, KINEMATIC_NECESSITY or
                            DECLARED_SCENARIO)
     MAINTAINED_BY_CLASS  - the joint class holds it by construction
     IRRELEVANT_BECAUSE   - name a scenario in which this DOF is BOTH unloaded
                            AND unactuated. If you cannot name one, it is not
                            irrelevant.
   Leaving a line out is the failure this stage exists to prevent.
6. For every LOAD CASE, trace the ordered PATH from where the load is applied,
   through THIS mechanism, to the reaction site. Each hop names a body or joint.
   A path that does not reach the reaction site is a load that is not reacted.
   Do not state how much load any element carries: that depends on dimensions
   that do not exist.
7. Give the ASSEMBLY ORDER. For each step: which body, from which ACCESS SIDE,
   what it depends on, and - if that body must stay put afterwards - which
   RETENTION TERMINATION holds it: LATER_BODY_COVER, ROTATION or ELASTICITY. A
   rigid part pushed straight in always leaves the reverse direction open, so
   one of those three is always needed. Mark the step DEFORMATION_RESOLVED if it
   only goes together because something flexes; otherwise RIGID.
8. Name the FUNCTIONAL REGIONS the design promises: ACCESS, SUPPORT, KEEP_OUT,
   APERTURE, and which bodies own them.
9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be
empty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.

  bodies[]             id "BOD-0001", role, instance_identity
  rigid_groups[]       id "RGP-0001", body, members[], is_default (boolean)
  joints[]             id "JNT-0001", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,
                       dof[], axis_direction,
                       compliance {mode, direction, required_travel,
                       allowable_travel_status, actuation, compliant_element,
                       root_interface, activation_window} (only for COMPLIANT)
  interfaces[]         id "IFC-0001", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal_status
  configurations[]     id "CFG-0001", name, kind, bodies_present[]

  load_paths[]         id "LDP-0001", load_case, candidate, ordered_hops[]
  assembly_steps[]     id "ASM-0001", order_index (integer), body, access_side,

request.prompt_text:
You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,
how they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,
and in what order the thing goes together.

You receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.

WHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT
Geometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies
touch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a
part is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and
no axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not
exist yet. Saying "the axis points +Z" is this stage's work. Saying "the axis is
40 mm from the base" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.

RULES
1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a
   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give
   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group
   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four
   groups and four joints, not one region.
2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of
   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.
3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify it
   as CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION. A body pair
   that meets and is left unclassified is a hole in the design.
4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism
   can be in that matter to its function.
5. DISPOSITION EVERY DEGREE OF FREEDOM. You are given the complete list below,
   one line per rigid group per configuration per DOF. Every line gets exactly
   one of:
     INTENDED             - this motion is the point
     BLOCKED_BY           - something stops it; say WHAT, in WHICH DIRECTION,
                            and HOW A TEST WOULD DEFEAT IT, and WHY it must be
                            blocked (LOAD, KINEMATIC_NECESSITY or
                            DECLARED_SCENARIO)
     MAINTAINED_BY_CLASS  - the joint class holds it by construction
     IRRELEVANT_BECAUSE   - name a scenario in which this DOF is BOTH unloaded
                            AND unactuated. If you cannot name one, it is not
                            irrelevant.
   Leaving a line out is the failure this stage exists to prevent.
6. For every LOAD CASE, trace the ordered PATH from where the load is applied,
   through THIS mechanism, to the reaction site. Each hop names a body or joint.
   A path that does not reach the reaction site is a load that is not reacted.
   Do not state how much load any element carries: that depends on dimensions
   that do not exist.
7. Give the ASSEMBLY ORDER. For each step: which body, from which ACCESS SIDE,
   what it depends on, and - if that body must stay put afterwards - which
   RETENTION TERMINATION holds it: LATER_BODY_COVER, ROTATION or ELASTICITY. A
   rigid part pushed straight in always leaves the reverse direction open, so
   one of those three is always needed. Mark the step DEFORMATION_RESOLVED if it
   only goes together because something flexes; otherwise RIGID.
8. Name the FUNCTIONAL REGIONS the design promises: ACCESS, SUPPORT, KEEP_OUT,
   APERTURE, and which bodies own them.
9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be
empty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.

purpose: turn a candidate family into a mechanism topology with a total DOF disposition

request.prompt_text:
You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,
how they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,
and in what order the thing goes together.

You receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.

WHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT
Geometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies
touch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a
part is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and
no axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not
exist yet. Saying "the axis points +Z" is this stage's work. Saying "the axis is
40 mm from the base" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.

RULES
1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a
   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give
   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group
   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four
   groups and four joints, not one region.
2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of
   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.
3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify it
   as CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION. A body pair
   that meets and is left unclassified is a hole in the design.
4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism
   can be in that matter to its function.
5. DISPOSITION EVERY DEGREE OF FREEDOM. You are given the complete list below,
   one line per rigid group per configuration per DOF. Every line gets exactly
   one of:
     INTENDED             - this motion is the point
     BLOCKED_BY           - something stops it; say WHAT, in WHICH DIRECTION,
                            and HOW A TEST WOULD DEFEAT IT, and WHY it must be
                            blocked (LOAD, KINEMATIC_NECESSITY or
                            DECLARED_SCENARIO)
     MAINTAINED_BY_CLASS  - the joint class holds it by construction
     IRRELEVANT_BECAUSE   - name a scenario in which this DOF is BOTH unloaded
                            AND unactuated. If you cannot name one, it is not
                            irrelevant.
   Leaving a line out is the failure this stage exists to prevent.
6. For every LOAD CASE, trace the ordered PATH from where the load is applied,
   through THIS mechanism, to the reaction site. Each hop names a body or joint.
   A path that does not reach the reaction site is a load that is not reacted.
   Do not state how much load any element carries: that depends on dimensions
   that do not exist.
7. Give the ASSEMBLY ORDER. For each step: which body, from which ACCESS SIDE,
   what it depends on, and - if that body must stay put afterwards - which
   RETENTION TERMINATION holds it: LATER_BODY_COVER, ROTATION or ELASTICITY. A
   rigid part pushed straight in always leaves the reverse direction open, so
   one of those three is always needed. Mark the step DEFORMATION_RESOLVED if it
   only goes together because something flexes; otherwise RIGID.
8. Name the FUNCTIONAL REGIONS the design promises: ACCESS, SUPPORT, KEEP_OUT,
   APERTURE, and which bodies own them.
9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be
empty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.

  bodies[]             id "BOD-0001", role, instance_identity
  rigid_groups[]       id "RGP-0001", body, members[], is_default (boolean)
  joints[]             id "JNT-0001", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,
                       dof[], axis_direction,
                       compliance {mode, direction, required_travel,
                       allowable_travel_status, actuation, compliant_element,
                       root_interface, activation_window} (only for COMPLIANT)
  interfaces[]         id "IFC-0001", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal_status
  configurations[]     id "CFG-0001", name, kind, bodies_present[]
  dof_dispositions[]   rigid_group, configuration, dof, disposition,

  load_paths[]         id "LDP-0001", load_case, candidate, ordered_hops[]
  assembly_steps[]     id "ASM-0001", order_index (integer), body, access_side,

request.prompt_text:
You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,
how they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,
and in what order the thing goes together.

You receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.

WHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT
Geometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies
touch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a
part is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and
no axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not
exist yet. Saying "the axis points +Z" is this stage's work. Saying "the axis is
40 mm from the base" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.

RULES
1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a
   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give
   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group
   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four
   groups and four joints, not one region.
2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of
   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.
3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify it
   as CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION. A body pair
   that meets and is left unclassified is a hole in the design.
4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism
   can be in that matter to its function.
5. DISPOSITION EVERY DEGREE OF FREEDOM. You are given the complete list below,
   one line per rigid group per configuration per DOF. Every line gets exactly
   one of:
     INTENDED             - this motion is the point
     BLOCKED_BY           - something stops it; say WHAT, in WHICH DIRECTION,
                            and HOW A TEST WOULD DEFEAT IT, and WHY it must be
                            blocked (LOAD, KINEMATIC_NECESSITY or
                            DECLARED_SCENARIO)
     MAINTAINED_BY_CLASS  - the joint class holds it by construction
     IRRELEVANT_BECAUSE   - name a scenario in which this DOF is BOTH unloaded
                            AND unactuated. If you cannot name one, it is not
                            irrelevant.
   Leaving a line out is the failure this stage exists to prevent.
6. For every LOAD CASE, trace the ordered PATH from where the load is applied,
   through THIS mechanism, to the reaction site. Each hop names a body or joint.
   A path that does not reach the reaction site is a load that is not reacted.
   Do not state how much load any element carries: that depends on dimensions
   that do not exist.
7. Give the ASSEMBLY ORDER. For each step: which body, from which ACCESS SIDE,
   what it depends on, and - if that body must stay put afterwards - which
   RETENTION TERMINATION holds it: LATER_BODY_COVER, ROTATION or ELASTICITY. A
   rigid part pushed straight in always leaves the reverse direction open, so
   one of those three is always needed. Mark the step DEFORMATION_RESOLVED if it
   only goes together because something flexes; otherwise RIGID.
8. Name the FUNCTIONAL REGIONS the design promises: ACCESS, SUPPORT, KEEP_OUT,
   APERTURE, and which bodies own them.
9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be
empty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.

  joints[]             id "JNT-0001", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,

  interfaces[]         id "IFC-0001", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal_status

request.prompt_text:
You are defining the MECHANISM for one candidate: what bodies exist,
how they are connected, what may move, what must not, how loads reach the world,
and in what order the thing goes together.

You receive the typed design state. You do not receive the original request.

WHAT EXISTS HERE AND WHAT DOES NOT
Geometry appears at this stage, but only as TOPOLOGY and DIRECTION: which bodies
touch, which joint connects which groups, which way an axis points, which side a
part is inserted from. There are no magnitudes, no dimensions, no positions and
no axis PLACEMENTS - where an axis sits depends on feature sizes that do not
exist yet. Saying "the axis points +Z" is this stage's work. Saying "the axis is
40 mm from the base" is not, and is wrong here even if it later turns out true.

RULES
1. Name the BODIES. A body is a thing that gets made or bought. Give each a
   ROLE - what it does - not a shape. Where a body must flex to do its job, give
   it more than one RIGID GROUP and a COMPLIANT joint between them: ONE group
   and ONE compliant joint PER COMPLIANT MEMBER. Four independent tabs are four
   groups and four joints, not one region.
2. Name every JOINT: its type, the two groups it connects, its degrees of
   freedom, and its axis DIRECTION.
3. Name every INTERFACE - every region where two bodies meet - and classify it
   as CONTACT, CLEARANCE, INTERFERENCE_FIT or COMPLIANT_INTERACTION. A body pair
   that meets and is left unclassified is a hole in the design.
4. Name the CONFIGURATIONS the product has - the distinct states its mechanism
   can be in that matter to its function.
5. DISPOSITION EVERY DEGREE OF FREEDOM. You are given the complete list below,
   one line per rigid group per configuration per DOF. Every line gets exactly
   one of:
     INTENDED             - this motion is the point
     BLOCKED_BY           - something stops it; say WHAT, in WHICH DIRECTION,
                            and HOW A TEST WOULD DEFEAT IT, and WHY it must be
                            blocked (LOAD, KINEMATIC_NECESSITY or
                            DECLARED_SCENARIO)
     MAINTAINED_BY_CLASS  - the joint class holds it by construction
     IRRELEVANT_BECAUSE   - name a scenario in which this DOF is BOTH unloaded
                            AND unactuated. If you cannot name one, it is not
                            irrelevant.
   Leaving a line out is the failure this stage exists to prevent.
6. For every LOAD CASE, trace the ordered PATH from where the load is applied,
   through THIS mechanism, to the reaction site. Each hop names a body or joint.
   A path that does not reach the reaction site is a load that is not reacted.
   Do not state how much load any element carries: that depends on dimensions
   that do not exist.
7. Give the ASSEMBLY ORDER. For each step: which body, from which ACCESS SIDE,
   what it depends on, and - if that body must stay put afterwards - which
   RETENTION TERMINATION holds it: LATER_BODY_COVER, ROTATION or ELASTICITY. A
   rigid part pushed straight in always leaves the reverse direction open, so
   one of those three is always needed. Mark the step DEFORMATION_RESOLVED if it
   only goes together because something flexes; otherwise RIGID.
8. Name the FUNCTIONAL REGIONS the design promises: ACCESS, SUPPORT, KEEP_OUT,
   APERTURE, and which bodies own them.
9. Do not select between candidates and do not score anything.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return a single JSON object with exactly these keys, each a list. A list may be
empty. Every field is required unless marked optional. No required field is null.

  bodies[]             id "BOD-0001", role, instance_identity
  rigid_groups[]       id "RGP-0001", body, members[], is_default (boolean)
  joints[]             id "JNT-0001", joint_type, parent_group, child_group,
                       dof[], axis_direction,
                       compliance {mode, direction, required_travel,
                       allowable_travel_status, actuation, compliant_element,
                       root_interface, activation_window} (only for COMPLIANT)
  interfaces[]         id "IFC-0001", bodies[], interaction_kind, nominal_status
  configurations[]     id "CFG-0001", name, kind, bodies_present[]
  dof_dispositions[]   rigid_group, configuration, dof, disposition,

                       scenario  (required when IRRELEVANT_BECAUSE),
                       holding_class (required when MAINTAINED_BY_CLASS)
  load_paths[]         id "LDP-0001", load_case, candidate, ordered_hops[]
  assembly_steps[]     id "ASM-0001", order_index (integer), body, access_side,
